verdict.rationale: Lium's own docs show you can pick a GPU type when renting, with an explicit `--gpu H100` example. It is described as a marketplace for renting NVIDIA GPUs by the hour, and you can rent the cheapest node matching a GPU spec. However, the pack never names H200 or B200, and never names any cheaper previous-generation model, so the breadth of choice the story asks for is not shown. Missing for 10: evidence of H200/B200 availability, evidence of named previous-generation options (e.g. A100/A6000-class) at lower prices, independent or hands-on confirmation of the GPU catalog.

support.subject: As an ML engineer, I can choose from current-generation datacenter GPUs (H100/H200/B200 class) as well as cheaper previous-generation options

citations.quote: Lium (lium.io) is a GPU rental marketplace: rent NVIDIA GPUs by the hour, billed per second.
